title: Stallion India Fluorochemicals Ltd. (NSE: STALLION) — Company Dossier
primer: We downgrade Stallion to a hard rejection for new capital after November 2026 filings broke its core thesis. Both Bhilwara R-32 and Mambattu slipped out of FY27 with overruns, while H1 cash flow fell to −₹39.17 crore. CARE Ratings flagged IPO deviation and commingling, GST officers cited five tax breaches, and promoter stake fell 20.1 points. At ₹171.59 on 25 November live TradingView (vs ₹180.48 on 23 November NSE ledger), the stock sits in Stage 4 below its 200-day line. Removing spent cash drops FY28 base value to ₹143.2 and weighted value to ₹132.9—so ₹155.07–₹159.79 is strictly a diagnostic technical pivot shelf, not a fundamental buy zone.
holding_rationale: Stallion is not held in any account in the 23 November 2026 positions ledger, so there are zero shares to sell and no active stop to manage. New capital is firmly rejected at zero allocation across all horizons because operational KPI health failed, Stage 4 technical structure broke below the 200-day average at ₹171.59, and re-underwritten FY28 base value (₹143.2) sits below both market price and the ₹155.07 to ₹159.79 diagnostic pivot shelf. Keep 100% of marginal capital in cash.

horizons.rationale: Stage 4 downtrend at ₹171.59 (25 Nov live TradingView) below the 200-day average (₹183.54) and all daily/weekly averages, with 4-hour RSI at 27.5, seven ledger distribution days, and no NSE derivatives chain.

Bhilwara R-32 and Mambattu both slipped into FY28 with cost overruns and zero FY27 revenue, Q2 core operating margin compressed to 9.19%, H1 operating cash flow fell to −₹39.17 crore, and a ~₹200 crore incremental funding gap looms.

Failed governance and cash-conversion discipline—CARE Ratings IPO deviation and commingling, ₹129 crore unmapped cost-plus-10% EPC advances, GST Section 67 contraventions, 20.1-point promoter stake drop, and CEO dismissal of cash flow—disqualify compounding underwriting.
